newsitem.title: SPAIN: Human error blamed for Spain's fatal train crashes.
newsitem.headline: Human error blamed for Spain's fatal train crashes.

text.p: Two train disasters that killed 20 people in Spain last week were due to driver errors which caused the trains to hit track switches at high speeds and derail, state railway Renfe said in a report on Thursday.
The two derailments happened only hours apart on March 31 in the northern Navarre region and on April 1 near Madrid, raising serious questions about the safety of Spain's railways.
In both cases, Renfe said there was no mechanical failure. But the conductors ignored signals warning them to slow down ahead of a switch from one track to another.
"The conductors...did not respect the signalling and in consequence, reached the switches at much higher speeds than those established for this type of shunting," the report said.

The train in Navarre, in which 18 people died and about 100 were injured, was travelling 137 km (85 miles) per hour in a 30 km (20 mile) zone. The train near Madrid, in which two people died, was going 150 kph in a 50 kph zone.
The engineers, who have been suspended from their jobs, have contested the report saying it was not thorough enough and aimed only at blaming the conductors.
"They have satanised the engineer, talking about driving vices so that what has happened is more digestible for public opinion," a spokesman for the engineers union told Reuters.
Renfe submitted its report to a court investigating the disasters which will make a final ruling on the causes.
